findings.title: SOQL Injection
findings.explanation: The method concatenates user input into a dynamic SOQL query string, which can lead to SOQL injection.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables or Database.queryWithBinds to safely include user input in SOQL queries.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The method does not enforce field-level security (FLS) for the Task object fields.
findings.remediation: Use Security.stripInaccessible to enforce FLS on the query results.

findings.title: SOQL Injection
findings.explanation: User input is concatenated directly into a dynamic SOQL query string, which can lead to SOQL injection.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables or String.escapeSingleQuotes to safely include user input in SOQL queries.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The query does not enforce field-level security (FLS) checks, which can allow users to access fields they do not have permission to view.
findings.remediation: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query to enforce FLS checks.

findings.title: SOSL injection
findings.explanation: User input is concatenated into a SOSL search term, allowing an attacker to inject malicious input.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables or String.escapeSingleQuotes to safely include user input in SOSL queries.

findings.title: SOQL Injection
findings.explanation: User input is concatenated directly into a SOQL query string, allowing an attacker to inject malicious SQL and access or modify data.
findings.remediation: Use bind variables or String.escapeSingleQuotes to safely include user input in SOQL queries.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The query does not enforce field-level security (FLS) checks, potentially allowing users to access fields they do not have permission to view.
findings.remediation: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query to enforce FLS.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The SOQL query does not enforce field-level security (FLS) with WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED, which could allow users to access fields they do not have permission to view.
findings.remediation: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query to enforce field-level security.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The DML operation does not enforce object-level security (CRUD) with 'update as user', which could allow users to update records they do not have permission to modify.
findings.remediation: Use 'update as user' to enforce object-level security.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS Violation
findings.explanation: The method does not check if the user has delete permission on the specific Asset record.
findings.remediation: Use Security.stripInaccessible to enforce record-level delete permissions.

findings.title: Excessive Permissions
findings.explanation: The permission set grants access to the AssetRetirementService class, which could allow users to delete any asset they have access to, not just those they own.
findings.remediation: Ensure the permission set only grants necessary permissions and consider additional record-level security controls.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The Apex class does not enforce CRUD/FLS permissions, allowing users to update contact phone numbers even if they do not have edit permissions on the Contact object or Phone field.
findings.remediation: Use WITH USER_MODE in the SOQL query and update the contact record as the running user to enforce CRUD/FLS permissions.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The query runs in system mode, ignoring field-level security, and updates the Rating field without checking field-level permissions.
findings.remediation: Use WITH USER_MODE in the SOQL query and enforce field-level security with Security.stripInaccessible before updating the record.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The code does not check if the user has create permission on the Task object before inserting a follow-up task.
findings.remediation: Add a check for isCreateable(Task.SObjectType) before inserting the task.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The code does not check if the user has edit permission on the Case.Status field before updating the case status.
findings.remediation: Add a check for isUpdateable(Case.Status) before updating the case status.

findings.title: Excessive permissions
findings.explanation: The permission set grants access to the CaseEscalationService class, which allows users to escalate cases and create tasks, even though task creation permission is not granted.
findings.remediation: Remove the class access for CaseEscalationService from the permission set if task creation is not intended.

findings.title: Sharing not enforced
findings.explanation: The class is declared 'without sharing', which ignores record-level sharing rules. This could allow access to data that the executing user should not see.
findings.remediation: Since this class is not an entry point and is called only from a scheduled batch job, it should be declared 'with sharing' to enforce record-level sharing rules.

findings.title: Sharing not enforced
findings.explanation: The class is declared 'without sharing', which ignores record-level sharing rules. This can allow users to access Case records they should not see.
findings.remediation: Change the class declaration to 'public with sharing class CaseHistoryController' to enforce record-level sharing rules.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS not enforced
findings.explanation: The SOQL query does not use WITH USER_MODE or WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED, which means it ignores object and field permissions.
findings.remediation: Add 'WITH USER_MODE' to the SOQL query to enforce CRUD and FLS checks.

findings.title: Sharing Violation
findings.explanation: The class is declared 'without sharing', which means it ignores record-level sharing rules. This allows partner community users to see opportunities from all accounts, not just their own.
findings.remediation: Change the class declaration to 'public with sharing class FinancialDashboardController' to enforce record-level sharing rules.

findings.title: Sharing violation
findings.explanation: DataAggregator is declared 'without sharing', ignoring record-level sharing rules. This class is reachable via @AuraEnabled, allowing users to bypass sharing rules.
findings.remediation: Change the class declaration to 'with sharing' to enforce record-level sharing rules.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The SOQL query in getLeadSummary() uses WITH USER_MODE but the class is 'without sharing', which can lead to CRUD/FLS violations.
findings.remediation: Ensure the class is 'with sharing' to enforce CRUD/FLS checks properly.

findings.title: Excessive Permissions
findings.explanation: The permission set grants Modify All Data and View All Data, which are powerful system permissions that should only be granted to administrators or integration users with a clear need.
findings.remediation: Remove Modify All Data and View All Data from the permission set unless there is a clear need for these permissions.

findings.title: Excessive Permission
findings.explanation: The permission set grants 'ManageInternalUsers' which allows managing users, which is not necessary for reviewing and approving invoices.
findings.remediation: Remove 'ManageInternalUsers' from the permission set as it is not required for the stated purpose.

findings.title: Excessive Permissions
findings.explanation: The permission set grants 'ViewAllData' which is a powerful system permission that should only be granted to administrators or integration users with a clear need.
findings.remediation: Remove 'ViewAllData' from the permission set unless absolutely necessary and justified.

findings.title: Guest user exposure
findings.explanation: The PublicCatalogController class is accessible to guest users, who can call it through the Aura endpoint. This exposes the Product2 object data to unauthenticated users.
findings.remediation: Remove PublicCatalogController from the guest profile's classAccesses, or ensure it only returns data intended to be public and enforces USER_MODE.

findings.title: CRUD/FLS violation
findings.explanation: The query does not enforce field-level security (FLS) for the Product2 object. Guest users might be able to access fields they should not.
findings.remediation: Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query to enforce FLS.
